spatial_claims.claim: Points A, C, B, D are collinear in order A-C-B-D, with C the midpoint of AB and BD added beyond B
AD = AC + CB + BD (segment decomposition along the line), with AC = CB
Line AD is cut at B into segments AB and BD (B lies between A and D)
Line AB is cut at C into segments AC and CB (C lies between A and B)
CD = CB + BD (B lies between C and D)

configuration_map: All points lie on a single straight line in order A-C-B-D. C is the midpoint of segment AB (so AC = CB). D is a point on the ray from A through B, beyond B. The segments partition as: AD = AC + CB + BD, AB = AC + CB, CD = CB + BD. All rectangles and squares referenced in the proof (rect(AD,BD), rect(AB,BD), sq(BD), sq(CB), sq(CD)) are algebraic entities from Book 2 propositions, not constructed polygons in the plane. No auxiliary points are constructed off the line.
pass_reason: The proof is purely algebraic, manipulating rectangle and square identities from Book 2 propositions (2.1, 2.3, 2.4) applied to segments of a single line. All spatial claims concern collinear betweenness on one line and are trivially consistent with the arrangement A-C-B-D. There are no angle decompositions, no interior/exterior arguments, no ray orderings, and no off-line constructions that could produce spatial contradictions.
